title: acme-pipeline: which tables to trust
subtitle: What the checks, the quarantine and the run records show for 5 Oct – 4 Nov 2026. The ops records end on 4 Nov; nothing after that was available.

verdict.text: Do not use `silver.orders` or `gold.sales_daily`. Every order delivery since 3 Nov has failed to load because the amounts now arrive with a decimal comma, so `sales_daily` was last built on 2 Nov 07:35. Since 28 Oct a new store id, S-031, has also been held in quarantine because `ref/stores.csv` lacks it. That is about 110 order lines a day, 12% of the order lines. Fix `orders_amount_positive` first: `amount < amount` can never fail. Then add a check on the quarantine, which would have flagged S-031 on its first day.

sections.title: Verdict per table
sections.intro: As of the last day in the records, 4 Nov. Whether anything was fixed between 5 and 10 Nov is not in the data.

rows: The loads of 3 Nov (two attempts) and 4 Nov failed on `"18846,00"` and `"5388,00"`, so order days 2 and 3 Nov are missing. S-031 has 665 lines held out since 28 Oct. Its amount check cannot fail.
load failed 4 Nov 07:41; no check result on 3 or 4 Nov
Not built since 2 Nov 07:35 against an 08:00 SLA. Built from `silver.orders` with an inner join on `ref.stores`, so S-031 has been missing since 28 Oct too.
38 malformed e-mails on 4 Nov. It has warned on 31 of 31 days with 37–41 rows and nobody acted. Three customers have no tax id (78 quarantine rows).
No check at all. It loaded on 31 of 31 days, but casts `amount` directly, the same code that broke `silver.orders`. The finance cash plan reads it.
No check at all. It has the same direct `amount` cast. No reader in the query log.

Both checks passed on 31 of 31 days, could fail and were tried on bad data. Freshness is only seen once a day at 23:55, though, so a daytime outage would go unseen [high]. If the ERP has stock for S-031, it is dropped by the same join on `ref.stores` [med].
Loaded on 31 of 31 days. `invoices_amount_parsed` passed on 31 of 31 days and was tried on 15 Sep on three bad formats. It only catches empty amounts.

Loaded every delivery, including 3 and 4 Nov (1,038 and 1,013 rows). Its not-empty and key-unique checks passed on 31 of 31 days and were both tried on 20 Jul. It is raw: the S-031 lines and the comma amounts are in it, untyped.

items.title: Order load fails on every delivery since 3 Nov; gold.sales_daily is two days stale and nobody logged it
items.where: pipeline/silver/orders.sql:18; ops/runs.jsonl (3 Nov 07:40 and 09:14, 4 Nov 07:40); ops/incident-log.md:13
items.evidence: Three failed attempts, each `invalid input syntax for type numeric` on a comma amount. `build_sales_daily` was skipped on 3 and 4 Nov, `sales_daily_fresh` failed on both days, and the last build was 2 Nov 07:35. The 14 Sep invoice incident had the same cause, and its open item, "check the other ERP amount columns", was never closed. The 3 Nov retry at 09:12 changed nothing. The incident log has no entry after 14 Sep. Finance, the BI sales board, the store ops app, the franchise portal and the regional managers' report all read `sales_daily`: 744 queries each in the period for the four hourly readers, 31 for finance.
items.fix: Use `util.parse_amount(amount)` in `silver/orders.sql:18`, and the same in `silver/returns.sql:10` and `silver/payments.sql:9`. Then reload the deliveries from 3 Nov onward and rebuild `sales_daily`. Write up the incident. The pipeline-incident skill can trace it end to end.

items.title: S-031 has been held in quarantine since 28 Oct, about 12% of order lines, and no check watches the quarantine
items.where: checks/quarantine.yaml:4-8; ref/stores.csv (30 stores, last changed 8 Jun); pipeline/gold/sales_daily.sql:19; checks/silver.yaml:13
items.evidence: 665 lines over 6 deliveries (28 Oct – 2 Nov), 103 to 123 a day, against 0 before. `silver.orders` kept writing about 900 rows a day while bronze rose to about 1,020, so this is new volume, not a re-keyed store. These lines are missing from `silver.orders` and `gold.sales_daily`. `orders_every_store_ordered` reads the same `ref.stores`, so it cannot see a store the reference lacks. Nothing alerts on the quarantine.
items.fix: Confirm with operations what S-031 is, add its row to `ref/stores.csv` and reload the deliveries from 28 Oct. Add a check on `ops/quarantine.jsonl` that warns when a rule takes more than 10 rows a day and fails on a value not seen before.

items.title: orders_amount_positive cannot fail and was never tried on bad data
items.evidence: `amount < amount` is never true, so the query returns 0 rows whatever the data. Its 29 passes prove nothing, and `silver.orders` has no other check on amounts.
items.fix: Use the condition that was meant, `amount <= 0` (or `amount < 0` if zero-price lines are legitimate). Add a test case with one negative and one zero amount and see it fail.

items.title: customers_email_format warns every day and can never fail
items.evidence: It warned on 31 of 31 days with 37–41 rows. `fail_if: rows > 500` is about 12 times the observed level, so it never fires. A daily warning nobody acts on hides the day it gets worse. `gold.sales_daily` serves `customer_email` to finance for follow-ups.
items.fix: Correct the 37–41 addresses in the ERP and set `fail_if: rows > 0`. Until then, set `fail_if: rows > 45` so a rise shows.

items.title: A failed load leaves no check result, and nothing notices the gap
items.evidence: On 3 and 4 Nov the `silver.orders` checks simply did not run. Their silence looked the same as a pass, and only the downstream `sales_daily_fresh` turned red.
items.fix: Treat a scheduled check with no result for a run date as a failure, or add a freshness check on `silver.orders` itself (newest `load_date` = today).

items.title: stock_levels_fresh promises "any time of the day" but looks once at 23:55
items.evidence: It runs on the cron `55 23 * * *`. `refresh_stock` writes only failed runs, and none were written in the period. A refresh that stopped at 10:00 and recovered by 23:55 would be seen by neither. The job's purpose is current stock for the stores, and `stock_planner` queried it 54 times.
items.fix: Run the freshness check every 15 minutes in opening hours, or have `refresh_stock` write a heartbeat per run and check the largest gap.

items.title: silver.payments and silver.returns have no checks and the same direct amount cast
items.evidence: Both loaded on 31 of 31 days. The day the ERP switches their export to a decimal comma they will fail like `silver.orders`, or worse, load wrongly with no check to see it. The finance cash plan reads `silver.payments`.
items.fix: Switch both to `util.parse_amount`, and add an `amount is null` check and a not-empty check like the invoice ones, each with a test case.

items.title: The missing_tax_id quarantine does not seem to keep rows out of silver.customers
items.evidence: The quarantine file says flagged rows stay out of silver. `customers.sql` loads every row of `erp_replica.customers` with no quarantine filter, so the 3 customers are probably in `silver.customers` with a null `tax_id` [med]. Not one of the 3 is a store franchisee in `ref.stores`.
items.fix: Decide which is meant: filter them out in `customers.sql`, or call the rule a flag rather than a quarantine. Then get the 3 tax ids from the ERP.

blocks.text: The `silver.orders` checks have fewer results because the table did not load on 3 and 4 Nov. `orders_every_store_ordered` also skips the Monday deliveries, which carry Sunday's orders, by design (`days: mon-sat`). Every check has a definition and every result has a check: none is orphaned.

rows: 2 in the records (3, 4 Nov); still late on 10 Nov unless fixed [guess]
none in the job; the check says 15 min
0 seen, checked once a day at 23:55

blocks.text: Even on good days the 08:00 SLA of `sales_daily` is thin. The ERP file arrived late on 23 of 32 order runs (36–67 minutes after 06:30), and the build finished as late as 07:52 (5 Oct). A file 10 minutes later than usual misses the SLA.

sections.title: Quarantine
sections.intro: Two rules: `unknown_store_id` on order lines (810 rows) and `missing_tax_id` on customers (78 rows). The order rule jumped from 3–7 rows a day to 107–129 on 28 Oct, 103–123 of them S-031. Nothing was quarantined on 3 and 4 Nov because `silver.orders` failed before that step.

blocks.title: unknown_store_id: rows quarantined per delivery day, by store id
blocks.caption: S-031 is new on 28 Oct and makes up about 12% of each day's order lines since. S-000 is a steady trickle all period.

sections.title: What looked wrong but is fine

items: `orders_every_store_ordered` failed on 24 Oct with 4 rows. These are the four Szeged stores (S-027 to S-030), closed on 23 Oct for the Hungarian national holiday, as the result's note says. It passed on 25 Oct. This is the check working.

`wait_for_file` warned on 23 of 32 order runs. The ERP delivers late on working days, and since commit 3e47102 the job waits up to 180 minutes. `sales_daily` still made 08:00 on every day it was built.

`missing_tax_id` went from 2 to 3 rows a day on 20 Oct. That is one more customer, not a jump. The same 3 customers come back every day because `silver.customers` is reloaded in full. None is a store franchisee.
S-000 is not the jump: it held 3–7 rows a day for the whole period. What it is remains an open question (see below).
`refresh_stock` has no run records. This is by design (`record_runs: failures`): zero means no failed run was written.

sections.title: What this summary did not check

items: Anything after 4 Nov. The ops records end there, so whether the order load was fixed between 5 and 10 Nov is unknown. Look at the live `ops/runs.jsonl` before the meeting.
The warehouse itself. No query was run. Every count here comes from the run records, the check results and the quarantine file.
The money behind S-031's 665 lines: bronze is not in the repository. Line counts only.
Whether `util.parse_amount` reads every format correctly. `invoices_amount_parsed` only catches empty amounts, so a value parsed the wrong way would pass.
The bronze finance tables (`erp_invoices`, `erp_returns`, `erp_payments`), which have no checks.
Personal data served in gold (`customer_email` in `gold.sales_daily`, read by the franchise portal). That belongs to a data-review or data-product page.
The runbook says `load_erp_orders` runs at 05:00, but the job starts at 06:30 (docs/runbook.md:11, jobs/load_erp_orders.yaml:3).

facts.scope: Data quality of the acme-pipeline tables, from ops/checks.jsonl, ops/quarantine.jsonl and ops/runs.jsonl for 2026-10-05 to 2026-11-04, and the definitions in checks/
assumptions: The ops files are the export of 4 Nov; the state on 10 Nov may differ.
S-031 is a real new store or customer. This is inferred because silver kept its usual about 900 rows while bronze grew by about 110.
A quarantine date is the delivery date, so order days are one day earlier.
open: What is S-031, and who adds new stores to ref/stores.csv?
What is S-000? It has been 3–7 order lines a day for the whole period.
Was the order load fixed and reloaded after 4 Nov?
Does the missing_tax_id rule really keep the 3 customers out of silver.customers?
Does erp_replica.stock hold S-031 stock that gold.stock_levels drops?
